data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims a 44-comparator 13-input network exists but files simulation_refs: [] — the problem explicitly states 'a simulation described in prose with an empty simulation_refs channel is an unverified claim and will be criticized as such.' The mechanism describes an exhaustive search over 5-comparator insertion sequences into an optimal 12-input network, but this discriminating experiment is never actually filed as a sandboxed Python simulation. Without a running program that verifies the candidate against all 8192 binary vectors, the existence claim for a 44-comparator network is pure assertion. Additionally, the core reasoning commits a category error: ceil(log2(13))=4 is the lower bound for sequential binary insertion into a sorted list, but comparator networks execute comparators in parallel layers where the 0-1 principle demands simultaneous correctness across all binary vectors — the target's own countercondition acknowledges this distinction yet the main claim relies on the invalid bound. No dossier block ids are cited anywhere in the target.
